0530|         */*) mkdir -p "${profile%/*}" || return 1 ;;
0531|     esac

0533|         return 1

0535|     {
0536|         if [ -s "$profile" ] && ! ends_with_newline "$profile"; then
0537|             printf '\n'
0538|             printf '%s\n' "$MARKER_SEPARATOR"
0539|         fi

0562| # The current time in milliseconds, so the check can be timed. A ``date`` with
0563| # nanoseconds answers with them; one without that extension (macOS writes the
0564| # literal ``N``) falls back to the interpreter the installer already requires,
0565| # and to whole seconds only when nothing finer answers. A host with no usable
0566| # clock reports 0, and the verdict is then the recorded timeout alone.
0567| now_millis() {

0569|     case $stamp in
0570|         ''|*[!0-9]*) stamp= ;;
0571|     esac
0572|     if [ "${#stamp}" -ge 19 ]; then
0573|         printf '%s\n' "$((stamp / 1000000))"
0574|         return 0
0575|     fi
0576|     if [ -n "${PYTHON:-}" ]; then
0577|         stamp=$("$PYTHON" -c 'import time; print(int(time.time() * 1000))' 2>/dev/null) || stamp=
0578|         case $stamp in
0579|             ''|*[!0-9]*) stamp= ;;
0580|         esac
0581|         if [ -n "$stamp" ]; then
0582|             printf '%s\n' "$stamp"
0583|             return 0
0584|         fi
0585|     fi
0586|     stamp=$(date +%s 2>/dev/null) || stamp=
0587|     case $stamp in
0588|         ''|*[!0-9]*) stamp=0 ;;
0589|     esac
0590|     printf '%s\n' "$((stamp * 1000))"
0591| }

0634| # Every descendant of a process, one pid per line.
0635| process_tree() {

0637|         { parent[$1] = $2; ids[NR] = $1 }

0639|             frontier[0] = root
0640|             count = 1

0642|                 for (j = 1; j <= NR; j++) {
0643|                     pid = ids[j]
0644|                     if (parent[pid] == frontier[i] && !(pid in seen)) {
0645|                         seen[pid] = 1
0646|                         frontier[count] = pid
0647|                         count++
0648|                     }
0649|                 }
0650|             }
0651|             for (i = 1; i < count; i++) print frontier[i]
0652|         }'

0655| # Start the checked command in a process group of its own, and record that group
0656| # for the whole lifetime of the check: the command may exit at once while
0657| # something it started lives on in the same group. The launcher puts itself in a
0658| # new session, and so in a new process group, before it runs the command; the
0659| # group id is therefore its own pid. Python is already required to install the
0660| # client. A shell without it falls back to its own job control, and otherwise to
0661| # the descendant sweep alone.
0662| start_check() {
0663|     out=$1
0664|     shift
0665|     if [ -n "${PYTHON:-}" ] && "$PYTHON" -c 'import os' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
0666|         "$PYTHON" -c '
0667| import os, sys
0668| try:
0669|     os.setsid()
0670| except OSError:
0671|     try:
0672|         os.setpgid(0, 0)
0673|     except OSError:
0674|         pass
0675| try:
0676|     os.execvp(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[1:])
0677| except OSError:
0678|     os._exit(127)

0681|         set -m 2>/dev/null || true

0683|     fi

0685|     set +m 2>/dev/null || true

0688| }

0690| # Signal every member of a process group. The caller's own group is never
0691| # signalled, so a check that could not be placed in a group of its own cannot
0692| # make the cleanup reach the installer itself.
0693| signal_group() {
0694|     signal=$1
0695|     group=$2
0696|     case $group in
0697|         ''|*[!0-9]*) return 0 ;;
0698|     esac
0699|     own=
0700|     if command -v ps >/dev/null 2>&1; then
0701|         own=$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ') || own=
0702|     fi
0703|     if [ -n "$own" ] && [ "$group" = "$own" ]; then
0704|         return 0
0705|     fi
0706|     if kill -"$signal" "-$group" 2>/dev/null; then
0707|         return 0
0708|     fi
0709|     # A shell that cannot name a group signals its members one by one.
0710|     for pid in $(process_group "$group"); do
0711|         kill -"$signal" "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
0712|     done
0713|     return 0
0714| }

0716| # Stop what the checked command started. The dedicated process group is the
0717| # primary target: everything that stayed in it goes at once, on the success path
0718| # as well as on the timeout path. A sweep of the checked command's descendants
0719| # follows, so a descendant that left the group is reached as well.
0720| stop_check() {
0721|     signal=$1
0722|     signal_group "$signal" "$CHECK_GROUP"
0723|     if [ -n "$CHECK_CHILD" ]; then
0724|         for pid in $(process_tree "$CHECK_CHILD"); do
0725|             kill -"$signal" "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
0726|         done
0727|         kill -"$signal" "$CHECK_CHILD" 2>/dev/null || true
0728|     fi
0729|     return 0
0730| }

0732| # Release everything the bounded check owns: the watchdog, the checked process
0733| # group with the descendants that left it, and the private directory. It runs at
0734| # most once per check, so the exit trap and a signal trap cannot release the
0735| # same check twice and a second call is a no-op. Every piece of state the
0736| # release reads is cleared only after it has been used.
0737| cleanup_check() {
0738|     if [ -n "$CHECK_CLEANED" ]; then
0739|         return 0
0740|     fi
0741|     CHECK_CLEANED=1
0742|     if [ -n "$CHECK_WATCHER" ]; then
0743|         kill -TERM "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0744|         wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0745|         CHECK_WATCHER=
0746|     fi
0747|     if [ -n "$CHECK_GROUP" ] || [ -n "$CHECK_CHILD" ]; then
0748|         stop_check KILL
0749|         if [ -n "$CHECK_CHILD" ]; then
0750|             wait "$CHECK_CHILD" 2>/dev/null || true
0751|         fi
0752|         CHECK_GROUP=
0753|         CHECK_CHILD=
0754|     fi
0755|     if [ -n "$CHECK_DIR" ]; then
0756|         rm -rf "$CHECK_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
0757|         CHECK_DIR=
0758|     fi
0759|     return 0
0760| }

0767| # Wait, for a bounded moment, until the watchdog has recorded its decision in
0768| # the private check directory: ``timed-out`` when the bound had elapsed before
0769| # the checked command exited, ``finished`` when it saw the command gone first.
0770| # Status 0 means the decision is there, 1 that the watchdog did not answer
0771| # within DECISION_WAIT seconds. The decision says which stop to expect; it is
0772| # not the verdict, which is the time the check took (see ``bounded_run``). The
0773| # wait never depends on the checked command, so a watchdog that never answers
0774| # delays the installer by that fixed limit at most.
0775| await_decision() {
0776|     decision_dir=$1
0777|     waited=0
0778|     while :; do
0779|         if [ -e "$decision_dir/timed-out" ] || [ -e "$decision_dir/finished" ]; then
0780|             return 0
0781|         fi
0782|         if [ "$waited" -ge "$DECISION_WAIT" ]; then
0783|             return 1
0784|         fi
0785|         sleep 1 2>/dev/null || true
0786|         waited=$((waited + 1))
0787|     done
0788| }

0790| # Run a command under a hard time bound. ``timeout`` from GNU coreutils is not
0791| # required and is not used: the command runs in the background and a watchdog
0792| # stops it once the bound elapsed. The watchdog records ``timed-out`` in the
0793| # private directory before it starts the graceful stop, and ``finished`` when it
0794| # saw the command gone before the bound; that record says which stop to expect,
0795| # never what the verdict is. The installer times the check itself and reports a
0796| # timeout whenever the measured time reached the bound, so the ordering between
0797| # the command's own exit, the record and the read of the result cannot turn a
0798| # step that overran into a success. A command that finished inside the bound
0799| # keeps its own status, a nonzero one included. After the graceful stop the
0800| # watchdog forcefully stops the rest of the checked command's process group once
0801| # the grace period has passed. Nothing the function starts survives it.
0802| # CHECK_STATUS is 124 when the bound elapsed.
0803| #
0804| # The checked command leads a process group of its own (see ``start_check``), so
0805| # the group is what the cleanup signals, on the success path as much as on the
0806| # timeout path. Its three standard descriptors are redirected, so the group has
0807| # no terminal to hold it and cannot stop on a terminal access.
0808| bounded_run() {
0809|     limit=$1
0810|     shift
0811|     CHECK_STATUS=0
0812|     CHECK_OUTPUT=
0813|     CHECK_CLEANED=
0814|     CHECK_CHILD=
0815|     CHECK_GROUP=
0816|     if ! create_check_dir; then
0817|         return 1
0818|     fi
0819|     out=$CHECK_DIR/output
0820|     timed_out=$CHECK_DIR/timed-out
0821|     finished=$CHECK_DIR/finished
0822|     saved_umask=$(umask)
0823|     umask 077
0824|     if ! : > "$out"; then
0825|         umask "$saved_umask"
0826|         cleanup_check
0827|         return 1
0828|     fi
0829|     started=$(now_millis)
0830|     start_check "$out" "$@"
0831|     umask "$saved_umask"
0832|     child=$CHECK_CHILD
0833|     (
0834|         exec > /dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null
0835|         sleeper=
0836|         trap 'kill "$sleeper" 2>/dev/null || true; exit 0' TERM
0837|         elapsed=0
0838|         while [ "$elapsed" -lt "$limit" ]; do
0839|             sleep 1 &
0840|             sleeper=$!
0841|             wait "$sleeper" 2>/dev/null || true
0842|             sleeper=
0843|             elapsed=$((elapsed + 1))
0844|             if ! kill -0 "$child" 2>/dev/null; then
0845|                 # The command was gone inside the bound; record that so the
0846|                 # caller knows which stop to expect.
0847|                 : > "$finished" 2>/dev/null || true
0848|                 exit 0
0849|             fi
0850|         done
0851|         : > "$timed_out" 2>/dev/null || true
0852|         stop_check TERM
0853|         sleep "$VERIFY_GRACE" 2>/dev/null || true
0854|         stop_check KILL
0855|     ) &
0856|     CHECK_WATCHER=$!
0857|     wait "$child" || CHECK_STATUS=$?
0858|     ended=$(now_millis)
0859|     measured=$((ended - started))
0860|     if await_decision "$CHECK_DIR"; then
0861|         # The watchdog records its decision before it stops anything, so on
0862|         # the timeout path it may still own the graceful then the forceful
0863|         # stop; let it finish so nothing outlives the check.
0864|         wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0865|     else
0866|         # A watchdog that never answers is not allowed to hold the installer. A
0867|         # decision that never arrives is not evidence that the bound was kept;
0868|         # the measured time decides that below.
0869|         kill -KILL "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0870|         wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0871|     fi
0872|     # The verdict is the time the check took, never the presence of a record: a
0873|     # step that outlived the bound is a timeout even when it exited on its own
0874|     # before the timeout was recorded, and a step inside the bound keeps its own
0875|     # status, a nonzero one included.
0876|     if [ -e "$timed_out" ] || [ "$measured" -ge "$((limit * 1000))" ]; then
0877|         CHECK_STATUS=124
0878|     fi
0879|     CHECK_OUTPUT=$(cat "$out") || CHECK_OUTPUT=
0880|     # The check is released here, before any state the release reads is
0881|     # cleared: a successful check leaves nothing behind, exactly like a failed
0882|     # or a timed-out one.
0883|     cleanup_check
0884|     return 0
0885| }

0002| 
0003| The client declares one minimum supported engine version, asks the engine for
0004| its own version once per invocation, and refuses to use an engine that is

0006| """

0008| from __future__ import annotations
0009|

0018| # One runnable line that installs the client together with the engine it needs.
0019| INSTALL_INSTRUCTION = (

0025| def numeric_version(version: Any) -> Optional[Tuple[int, ...]]:
0026|     """The numeric components of a version, trailing zero components dropped.
0027| 
0028|     Components compare one at a time from the first, so a version with fewer
0029|     components equals the same version with trailing zero components, and a
0030|     non-numeric suffix after the numeric components affects nothing.
0031|     """
0032|     if version is None:
0033|         return None
0034|     text = str(version).strip()
0035|     if text[:1] in ("v", "V"):
0036|         text = text[1:]
0037|     components = []
0038|     for part in text.split("."):
0039|         digits = ""
0040|         for character in part.strip():
0041|             if not character.isdigit():
0042|                 break
0043|             digits += character
0044|         if not digits:
0045|             break
0046|         components.append(int(digits))
0047|     if not components:
0048|         return None
0049|     while len(components) > 1 and components[-1] == 0:
0050|         components.pop()
0051|     return tuple(components)
0052|

0055|     """The version the engine reports about itself, if it reports one."""
0056|     if not isinstance(payload, dict):
0057|         return None
0058|     engine = payload.get("engine")
0059|     if isinstance(engine, dict):
0060|         value = engine.get("version")
0061|         if value is not None and str(value).strip():
0062|             return str(value).strip()
0063|     value = payload.get("version")
0064|     if value is not None and str(value).strip():
0065|         return str(value).strip()
0066|     return None
0067|

0070|     """Whether ``version`` is at or above the declared minimum."""

0072|     required = numeric_version(minimum)
0073|     if found is None or required is None:

2069| def _quoted_binding(text: str, after: int) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int]]:
2070|     """The value bound to a quoted label, whose closing quote ends at ``after``.
2071| 
2072|     A quoted label binds its value through a separator, through a quoted run
2073|     next to it, or through the bare word that follows it when that word is a
2074|     value: one that closes the clause or carries value markers. A word that
2075|     merely continues the sentence mentions the quoted label instead.
2076|     """

2082|     if text[position] in _QUOTE_PAIRS:

2086|         return None

2090|         # ``'token' Bearer VALUE``: the scheme word stays, the value goes.
2091|         return _scheme_value(text, end)
2092|     if word in COPULAS:
2093|         # ``'token' is VALUE``: the copula stays, the word after decides.
2094|         return _copula_span(text, end)

2096|         # The quoted word is mentioned, not bound to a value.
2097|         return None
2098|     if not _carries_markers(token) and not _closes_clause(text, end):
2099|         # A plain word still followed by the sentence mentions the label.
2100|         return None

2104| def _binding(text: str, start: int, label_end: int) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int]]:
2105|     """The span of the value bound to the label that starts at ``start``."""
2106|     while True:
2107|         if label_end >= len(text):
2108|             return None
2109|         character = text[label_end]
2110|         if character in _QUOTE_PAIRS:
2111|             quoted = _label_quote_end(text, label_end)
2112|             if quoted is not None:
2113|                 # The quote closes the label, so the binding starts after it.
2114|                 return _quoted_binding(text, quoted)
2115|             return _span(text, label_end)
2116|         if character in "=:":
2117|             return _bound_value(text, _separator_end(text, label_end), True)
2118|         if character not in _WHITESPACE:
2119|             return None
2120|         after = _skip_gap(text, label_end)
2121|         if after >= len(text):
2122|             return None
2123|         if text[after] in "=:":
2124|             label_end = after
2125|             continue
2126|         if text[after] in _QUOTE_PAIRS:
2127|             # ``password "hunter2 and more"`` binds the quoted run.
2128|             return _span(text, after)
2129|         following = _label_end(text, after)
2130|         if following is None:
2131|             return None
2132|         word = _bare(text[after:following])
2133|         if word in AUTH_SCHEMES:
2134|             # ``token Bearer VALUE``: the scheme word stays, the value goes.
2135|             return _scheme_value(text, following)
2136|         if _secret_label(text[after:following]):
2137|             # A compound label may be written as several words.
2138|             label_end = following
2139|             continue
2140|         if word in COPULAS:
2141|             # ``the token is VALUE``: the copula stays, the word after decides.
2142|             return _copula_span(text, following)
2143|         if _is_prose(text[after:following]):
2144|             # The label is mentioned, not bound to a value.
2145|             return None
2146|         # An ordinary descriptor may stand between the label and its value.
2147|         return _descriptor_span(text, after)

2239| def resolve(text: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
2240|     """Decide which single action one sentence asks for.
2241| 
2242|     ``kind`` is one of ``leave``, ``sensitive``, ``switch``, ``plan``,
2243|     ``clarify``, ``action`` or ``say``.
2244|     """
2245|     stripped = text.strip()
2246|     lowered = _normalise(stripped)
2247| 
2248|     if lowered.strip(" !.?,:;") in LEAVE_WORDS:
2249|         return {"kind": "leave"}
2250| 
2251|     if any(marker in lowered for marker in SENSITIVE_MARKERS):
2252|         return {"kind": "sensitive"}
2253| 
2254|     # The French and Spanish phrasings of the same actions are compared folded:
2255|     # case, diacritics, punctuation and repeated whitespace carry no meaning.
2256|     if _asks_for_sensitive_action(_fold(stripped)):
2257|         return {"kind": "sensitive"}
2258| 
2259|     # English and Russian name the same actions with a verb and the object it
2260|     # acts on; only a sentence that names both asks for one of them.
2261|     if _asks_for_explicit_action(_fold(stripped)):
2262|         return {"kind": "sensitive"}
2263| 
2264|     # A switch prefix may end the sentence, so the line is compared with a
2265|     # trailing space: ``switch to`` still asks for a project key.
2266|     padded = lowered + " "
2267|     for prefix in SWITCH_PREFIXES:
2268|         if padded.startswith(prefix):
2269|             key = _switch_key(stripped, prefix)
2270|             if not key:
2271|                 return {"kind": "clarify", "reason": "clarify_project"}
2272|             return {"kind": "switch", "key": key}
2273| 
2274|     if lowered.strip(" !.?,:;") in PLAN_EXACT:
2275|         return {"kind": "plan", "goal": ""}
2276|     for prefix in PLAN_PREFIXES:
2277|         if lowered.startswith(prefix):
2278|             return {"kind": "plan", "goal": stripped[len(prefix):].strip()}
2279| 
2280|     tokens = stripped.split()
2281|     matched = [
2282|         name for name, words in ACTIONS if any(word in lowered for word in words)
2283|     ]
2284|     if len(matched) > 1:
2285|         return {"kind": "clarify", "reason": "clarify_several"}
2286|     if not matched:
2287|         if _task_id(tokens) is not None:
2288|             # The owner names a task but no action the session can carry out.
2289|             return {"kind": "clarify", "reason": "clarify_action"}
2290|         return {"kind": "say", "text": stripped}
2291| 
2292|     name = matched[0]
2293|     if name in ("pause", "resume"):
2294|         return {"kind": "action", "action": name}
2295| 
2296|     task_id = _task_id(tokens)
2297|     if task_id is None:
2298|         return {"kind": "clarify", "reason": "clarify_task"}
2299|     remarks = ""
2300|     if name == "rework":
2301|         index = next(
2302|             (
2303|                 position
2304|                 for position, token in enumerate(tokens)
2305|                 if token.strip("\"'`.,;:()").lstrip("#") == task_id
2306|             ),
2307|             None,
2308|         )
2309|         rest = " ".join(tokens[index + 1:]) if index is not None else ""
2310|         remarks = _remarks(rest)
2311|         if not remarks:
2312|             return {"kind": "clarify", "reason": "clarify_remarks"}
2313|     return {
2314|         "kind": "action",
2315|         "action": name,
2316|         "task": task_id,
2317|         "remarks": remarks,
2318|     }

0001| #!/bin/sh
0002| # Forgel Code installer.
0003| #
0004| # One command installs the client into a per-user prefix:
0005| #
0006| #   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh
0007| #
0008| # The client goes into ${FORGEL_CODE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share/forgel-code}, the
0009| # ``forgel-code`` launcher into ${FORGEL_CODE_BIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}, and that
0010| # directory is put on PATH through one marked block in the profile an
0011| # interactive login session of the login shell reads. The login shell is taken
0012| # from $SHELL, then from the invoking process (ps), then from the account login
0013| # shell; a shell outside the zsh and bash families gets the block in
0014| # $HOME/.profile and a warning that names the edited file. After writing the
0015| # block the installer starts that shell as a login interactive shell from a
0016| # cleared environment, in a process group of its own, under a hard time limit.
0017| # A watchdog stops that shell once the limit elapses, and the installer times
0018| # the check itself: a shell that outlived the limit fails the installation,
0019| # whatever the ordering of its own exit and the watchdog's timeout record. The
0020| # absence of a recorded timeout at the moment the check's result arrives is
0021| # never taken as evidence that the check kept its bound. Nothing the check
0022| # started outlives it: the dedicated group, and the descendants that left it,
0023| # are stopped on every exit path. The installer then checks that
0024| # ``forgel-code`` resolves to the launcher it just wrote. Re-running replaces
0025| # the installation; running with ``--uninstall`` removes it again.
0026| #
0027| # Installing the client alone is not enough to use it, so the same run also
0028| # makes sure an engine the client supports is in place. It asks the engine's own
0029| # installer which version the configured engine source provides, without
0030| # installing anything, and reads the version of an engine that is already
0031| # present. Only then does it decide: a present engine that satisfies the
0032| # client's minimum is kept when the available version is not strictly newer, a
0033| # strictly newer available engine replaces it, and an absent engine is obtained
0034| # when the available version is supported. Anything else ends the run as a
0035| # failure that names the required minimum, the version found or offered and the
0036| # action the user can take. A successful run always states the engine version in
0037| # place and how it was obtained. ``--client-only`` installs the client alone and
0038| # touches no engine. Reading a version report, and installing a version, are the
0039| # engine installer's own jobs; this script only decides and delegates.
0040| #
0041| # Environment variables:
0042| #   FORGEL_CODE_HOME            install prefix (default: $HOME/.local/share/forgel-code)
0043| #   FORGEL_CODE_BIN             launcher directory (default: $HOME/.local/bin)

0045| #   FORGEL_CODE_TAG             repository tag when no checkout is given (default: v0.2.0)

0054| #   FORGEL_ENGINE_INSTALLER     the engine's own installer (default: forgel-install on PATH)

0048|                 continue

0051|                 parts.append("%s=%s" % (key, value))

0001| # code
0002| 
0003| Forgel Code — thin console client for Forgel over the engine's machine-readable
0004| commands.
0005| 
0006| The client does not import the engine. Its only channel is running
0007| `forgel <command> --json` as a separate process and reading exactly one JSON
0008| object from stdout. The model, sandbox, independent QA, review and release
0009| approval stay in the engine: the client never calls a model, never reads
0010| project files and never runs checks itself.
0011| 
0012| ## Install
0013| 
0014| Forgel Code installs with one command. It needs Python 3.9 or newer with the
0015| `pip` module it ships. The same run also brings the `forgel` engine the client
0016| needs onto the machine, so one command leaves a working client-and-engine pair.
0017| 
0018| ```sh
0019| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh
0020| ```
0021| 
0022| The installer puts the client into `~/.local/share/forgel-code` and a
0023| `forgel-code` launcher into `~/.local/bin`, then adds that directory to `PATH`
0024| through one marked block in the profile your login shell reads. No virtual
0025| environment and no activation step are involved, and the same command run again
0026| replaces the installation instead of duplicating anything.
0027| 
0028| | Login shell | Profile file that receives the block |
0029| | --- | --- |
0030| | zsh | `~/.zshrc` |
0031| | bash | the first existing of `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`, `~/.profile`; `~/.bash_profile` is created when none of them exists |
0032| | other POSIX `sh` | `~/.profile`, with a warning on stderr that names the file and the detected shell |
0033| 
0034| The login shell comes from `$SHELL`. When that is unset, empty or names a shell
0035| the installer does not handle, it reads the shell of the invoking process and
0036| then the account login shell — the macOS Directory Service entry, otherwise the
0037| passwd entry — and only then falls back to `~/.profile`. The block is never
0038| written to `~/.bashrc` alone, because a login bash shell does not read that
0039| file. A profile file that does not exist yet is created.
0040| 
0041| The block carries a `case "$PATH:"` guard and prepends the launcher directory
0042| only when it is not already there, so sourcing it again, or sourcing several
0043| profiles that carry it, leaves exactly one entry. There is no unguarded
0044| `export PATH=...` line.
0045| 
0046| After writing the block the installer checks it: it starts the detected login
0047| shell as a login interactive shell from a cleared environment, under a bounded
0048| time limit enforced without GNU `timeout`, and requires `command -v forgel-code`
0049| to resolve to the launcher it just wrote. On success it prints the detected
0050| shell, the edited profile file and the path that fresh shell resolved. If the
0051| check fails, or the shell does not answer within the limit, it exits non-zero

0058| ### The engine
0059| 
0060| The same run settles the engine the client runs. It first learns which engine
0061| version the configured engine source offers, without installing anything, and
0062| which version of an engine is already in place. Then it decides:
0063| 
0064| | Engine in place | Offered version | Result |
0065| | --- | --- | --- |
0066| | none | at or above the declared minimum | that version is installed |
0067| | at or above the minimum, and the offered version is not strictly newer | any | the engine is kept and nothing about it is changed |
0068| | below the offered version | supported and strictly newer | the strictly newer version replaces the engine in place |
0069| 
0070| A version equal to, or older than, the one in place is never installed. The
0071| engine versions are ordered numerically, component by component; one leading
0072| version prefix and trailing zero components do not change the comparison, and a
0073| version that cannot be ordered never counts as supported. The engine left in
0074| place always satisfies the client's declared minimum supported engine version;
0075| when that cannot be reached the run ends as a failure instead of reporting the
0076| pair as installed: the offered version is below the minimum and no suitable
0077| engine is present, the engine source cannot be read, or installing the engine
0078| fails. The failure message names the required minimum, the engine version found
0079| or offered, and what you can do next. A successful run states the engine version
0080| in place and how it was obtained: installed, kept or replaced.

0083| 
0084| The engine source the run resolves against is configuration with a default, and
0085| either variable can point it elsewhere.
0086| 
0087| | Variable | Effect |
0088| | --- | --- |
0089| | `FORGEL_ENGINE_SOURCE` | engine source the run asks about and installs from (default `https://github.com/forgel-dev/forgel`) |
0090| | `FORGEL_ENGINE_INSTALLER` | the engine's own installer the run asks and delegates to (default `forgel-install` on `PATH`) |
0091| 
0092| ```sh
0093| FORGEL_ENGINE_SOURCE=https://example.test/forgel-mirror sh install.sh
0094| ```

0096| ### Client only
0097| 
0098| ```sh
0099| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh -s -- --client-only
0100| ```

0108| backend (`_build_backend.py`), so the installer never needs a package index.

0145| 
0146| ```sh

0148| ```

0151| the marked `PATH` block from every profile file this installer can have written:
0152| `~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`, `~/.zshenv`, `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`,
0153| `~/.profile` and `~/.bashrc`. When `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` names another file, the

0155| behind by an install that edited a custom profile — including an install that
0156| wrote the block and then failed its fresh-shell check — does not survive. A file
0157| that is missing or carries no marker is left alone, no file is created, and the

0161| Windows is not the main installation method; the fallback there is `python -m pip install --user` of the pinned revision.
0162| 
0163| ## Interactive session
0164| 
0165| Starting `forgel-code` with no arguments opens an interactive session instead of
0166| printing usage text. It shows a prompt and stays open until you leave, so you
0167| work by writing sentences rather than by translating every intent into a
0168| command.
0169| 
0170| Each sentence is handed to the engine's project agent as one free-form request
0171| and the agent's answer is shown in the session. The session also shows the
0172| project it is working on, and re-reads the task and release state from the
0173| engine on its own, so progress becomes visible without asking for a status
0174| again.
0175| 
0176| Some sentences ask the session for one specific action:
0177| 
0178| | You write | What the session asks the engine for |
0179| | --- | --- |
0180| | a plain sentence | the project agent's answer |
0181| | `plan <goal>` | a plan for the goal, shown with its tasks in plan order and their states |
0182| | `accept <task>` | accepting that task |
0183| | `rework <task> <remarks>` | sending that task back with the remarks |
0184| | `retry <task>` | retrying that task |
0185| | `pause` | pausing work |
0186| | `resume` | resuming work |
0187| | `switch to <key>` | selecting another project; every later request and every later state shown uses the new project |
0188| | `leave`, `exit`, `quit`, or the end of the input | ending the session |
0189| 
0190| A sentence that names no action, or more than one, gets a clarification and
0191| nothing is carried out. A request that becomes a plan shows its tasks in plan
0192| order, and one that becomes a task shows that task with its title and state.
0193| When an engine call fails, the session shows the reason and the next possible
0194| step and stays usable for the next request; leaving after a failure needs no
0195| restart. Replies follow the language of your message.
0196| 
0197| Adopting a repository, creating a project, setting or changing a secret and
0198| changing configuration are not part of the conversation. A sentence never
0199| carries them out; the session only points you to the explicit command for them.
0200| 
0201| Leaving ends the session at once: the client sends nothing further to the
0202| engine and keeps no transcript. Key material never reaches the screen, because
0203| a value that names a secret is replaced before it is shown.
0204| 
0205| The interactive session adds no capability of its own: every answer and every
0206| piece of state comes from the engine, and the client still calls no model, reads
0207| no project and runs no check. All commands below keep working one-shot, with the
0208| same output, exit status and `--json` form as before.
0209| 
0210| ## Commands
0211| 
0212| Every client command is a thin wrapper over an existing engine command, and
0213| the engine is always called with `--json`. `<key>` below is the project the
0214| client session selected with `forgel-code use`; while nothing is selected the
0215| client passes no `--project` and the engine keeps its own active project.
0216| 
0217| | Client command | Engine command | Purpose |
0218| | --- | --- | --- |
0219| | `forgel-code say <phrase>` | `forgel say "<phrase>"` | Turn a free phrase into a task |
0220| | `forgel-code status` | `forgel status` | State of the task and the milestone |
0221| | `forgel-code tasks` | `forgel tasks` | List tasks |
0222| | `forgel-code task <task>` | `forgel tasks` | State of one task, picked out of the engine's task list |
0223| | `forgel-code accept <task>` | `forgel task accept --task <task> [--project <key>]` | Accept a task |
0224| | `forgel-code rework <task> <remark...>` | `forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" [--project <key>]` | Send a task back for rework with remarks |
0225| | `forgel-code resume` | `forgel resume` | Start or resume work |
0226| | `forgel-code pause` | `forgel pause` | Pause work |
0227| | `forgel-code plan "<goal>" [--milestone <key>]` | `forgel plan [<key>] --goal "<goal>"` | Decompose the milestone goal into tasks |
0228| | `forgel-code history` | `forgel history` | Short session history |
0229| | `forgel-code projects` | `forgel projects` | List projects |
0230| | `forgel-code session` | `forgel session` | Show the session the engine reports |
0231| | `forgel-code use <key>` | `forgel use <key>` | Select the active project |
0232| 
0233| `forgel-code` does not read a project itself: `task <task>` asks the engine for
0234| its task list and shows the one task you named. If that task is not in the
0235| engine's answer — or appears there more than once — the client reports it and
0236| exits with a non-zero code.
0237| 
0238| `accept` and `rework` lean on the engine's `task` command and its positional
0239| actions: accepting is `task accept`, sending back is `task reject`, and the
0240| remarks travel in the engine's `--notes`. The client adds no subcommand and no
0241| option of its own. The exact engine calls behind them are:
0242| 
0243| ```sh
0244| forgel task accept --task <task> --json
0245| forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" --json
0246| ```
0247| 
0248| When the running engine does not provide the action a point needs, the client
0249| prints the engine's own message plus an explicit note ("no engine command for
0250| this point") and exits with a non-zero code instead of inventing behaviour.
0251| That decision is taken from the engine's return code and structured error
0252| fields, never from the wording of its message, so it does not depend on the
0253| locale.
0254| 
0255| ### Output
0256| 
0257| Without a flag a command prints human readable text. With `--json` it prints
0258| exactly one JSON object to stdout:
0259| 
0260| ```json
0261| {"command": "status", "project": "acme", "ok": true, "result": {}}
0262| ```
0263| 
0264| The `project` field is the project key actually handed to the engine, or `null`
0265| when nothing was passed. On failure — including an argument-parse error — the
0266| client exits with a non-zero code and, with `--json`, prints one JSON object
0267| with `"ok": false` and the message under `error`. A structured engine refusal
0268| (`"ok": false` in the engine's answer) is a failure even when the engine exits
0269| with code 0, and its own fields are carried through. A failure report names the
0270| engine that answered: the path configured by `--engine`, `$FORGEL_ENGINE` or
0271| `forgel` leads the message.
0272| 
0273| ### Active project
0274| 
0275| `forgel-code use <key>` hands the key to the engine and, only when the engine
0276| accepts it, makes it the active project; every project-scoped command then
0277| passes `--project <key>`. `forgel-code projects` lists what the engine knows
0278| about. Until you pick a key no `--project` argument is sent, so the engine's own
0279| active project is used. Set `FORGEL_CODE_HOME` to move the session file.
0280| 
0281| ### Timeout
0282| 
0283| The engine call is bounded. `--timeout SECONDS` sets the limit for one call,
0284| `$FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT` sets it for the environment, and the default is 600
0285| seconds. When the limit elapses the client kills the engine and fails with a
0286| structured error instead of blocking. The engine's stdout is always decoded as
0287| UTF-8 and the child process does not receive the client's stdin.
0288| 
0289| `--json`, `--engine` and `--timeout` are parsed as options of their own and are
0290| never substituted inside argument text, so a phrase or remark that mentions
0291| such a word reaches the engine unchanged. Put `--` before a remark that itself
0292| begins with a hyphen.
0293|

0797| # the command's own exit, the record and the read of the result cannot turn a
0798| # step that overran into a success. A command that finished inside the bound
0799| # keeps its own status, a nonzero one included. After the graceful stop the
0800| # watchdog forcefully stops the rest of the checked command's process group once

0002| # Forgel Code installer.
0003| #
0004| # One command installs the client into a per-user prefix:
0005| #
0006| #   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh
0007| #
0008| # The client goes into ${FORGEL_CODE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share/forgel-code}, the
0009| # ``forgel-code`` launcher into ${FORGEL_CODE_BIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}, and that
0010| # directory is put on PATH through one marked block in the profile an
0011| # interactive login session of the login shell reads. The login shell is taken
0012| # from $SHELL, then from the invoking process (ps), then from the account login
0013| # shell; a shell outside the zsh and bash families gets the block in
0014| # $HOME/.profile and a warning that names the edited file. After writing the
0015| # block the installer starts that shell as a login interactive shell from a
0016| # cleared environment, in a process group of its own, under a hard time limit.
0017| # A watchdog stops that shell once the limit elapses, and the installer times
0018| # the check itself: a shell that outlived the limit fails the installation,
0019| # whatever the ordering of its own exit and the watchdog's timeout record. The
0020| # absence of a recorded timeout at the moment the check's result arrives is
0021| # never taken as evidence that the check kept its bound. Nothing the check
0022| # started outlives it: the dedicated group, and the descendants that left it,
0023| # are stopped on every exit path. The installer then checks that
0024| # ``forgel-code`` resolves to the launcher it just wrote. Re-running replaces
0025| # the installation; running with ``--uninstall`` removes it again.
0026| #
0027| # Installing the client alone is not enough to use it, so the same run also
0028| # makes sure an engine the client supports is in place. It asks the engine's own
0029| # installer which version the configured engine source provides, without
0030| # installing anything, and reads the version of an engine that is already
0031| # present. Only then does it decide: a present engine that satisfies the
0032| # client's minimum is kept when the available version is not strictly newer, a
0033| # strictly newer available engine replaces it, and an absent engine is obtained
0034| # when the available version is supported. Anything else ends the run as a
0035| # failure that names the required minimum, the version found or offered and the
0036| # action the user can take. A successful run always states the engine version in
0037| # place and how it was obtained. ``--client-only`` installs the client alone and
0038| # touches no engine. Reading a version report, and installing a version, are the
0039| # engine installer's own jobs; this script only decides and delegates.

0002| """The deterministic fake of the engine's own installer.
0003| 
0004| ``install.sh`` consumes two abilities the engine owns and never reimplements:
0005| it asks which engine version a source provides without installing anything, and
0006| it asks for one version to be installed. Both are served here, exactly as the
0007| dependency contract records them.
0008| 
0009| Contract:
0010| 
0011|   forgel-install --source SOURCE --available-version
0012|       Prints the engine version SOURCE provides on stdout and exits 0. It
0013|       installs nothing.
0014| 
0015|   forgel-install --source SOURCE --install VERSION
0016|       Installs VERSION and exits 0, or prints why on stderr and exits non-zero.
0017| 
0018| The engine binary the installer writes answers the engine's own report,
0019| ``forgel --version --json``, with one JSON object on stdout.
0020| 
0021| State, so a scenario can force any case:
0022| 
0023|   FORGEL_STUB_ENGINE_AVAILABLE       version the source provides (default 0.0.0)
0024|   FORGEL_STUB_ENGINE_SOURCES         file of "source version" lines; overrides
0025|   FORGEL_STUB_ENGINE_AVAILABLE_EXIT  exit code of --available-version
0026|   FORGEL_STUB_ENGINE_INSTALL_EXIT    exit code of --install
0027|   FORGEL_STUB_ENGINE_TARGET          path of the engine binary to write

0029| """

0562| # The current time in milliseconds, so the check can be timed. A ``date`` with
0563| # nanoseconds answers with them; one without that extension (macOS writes the
0564| # literal ``N``) falls back to the interpreter the installer already requires,
0565| # and to whole seconds only when nothing finer answers. A host with no usable
0566| # clock reports 0, and the verdict is then the recorded timeout alone.
0567| now_millis() {

0573|         printf '%s\n' "$((stamp / 1000000))"

0575|     fi

0579|             ''|*[!0-9]*) stamp= ;;
0580|         esac
0581|         if [ -n "$stamp" ]; then
0582|             printf '%s\n' "$stamp"
0583|             return 0
0584|         fi
0585|     fi
0586|     stamp=$(date +%s 2>/dev/null) || stamp=

0588|         ''|*[!0-9]*) stamp=0 ;;
0589|     esac
0590|     printf '%s\n' "$((stamp * 1000))"

0635| process_tree() {

0637|         { parent[$1] = $2; ids[NR] = $1 }
0638|         END {
0639|             frontier[0] = root
0640|             count = 1
0641|             for (i = 0; i < count; i++) {
0642|                 for (j = 1; j <= NR; j++) {
0643|                     pid = ids[j]
0644|                     if (parent[pid] == frontier[i] && !(pid in seen)) {
0645|                         seen[pid] = 1
0646|                         frontier[count] = pid
0647|                         count++
0648|                     }
0649|                 }
0650|             }

0655| # Start the checked command in a process group of its own, and record that group
0656| # for the whole lifetime of the check: the command may exit at once while
0657| # something it started lives on in the same group. The launcher puts itself in a
0658| # new session, and so in a new process group, before it runs the command; the
0659| # group id is therefore its own pid. Python is already required to install the
0660| # client. A shell without it falls back to its own job control, and otherwise to
0661| # the descendant sweep alone.
0662| start_check() {
0663|     out=$1
0664|     shift
0665|     if [ -n "${PYTHON:-}" ] && "$PYTHON" -c 'import os' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
0666|         "$PYTHON" -c '
0667| import os, sys
0668| try:
0669|     os.setsid()
0670| except OSError:
0671|     try:
0672|         os.setpgid(0, 0)
0673|     except OSError:
0674|         pass
0675| try:
0676|     os.execvp(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[1:])
0677| except OSError:
0678|     os._exit(127)

0681|         set -m 2>/dev/null || true

0683|     fi

0685|     set +m 2>/dev/null || true

0688| }

0690| # Signal every member of a process group. The caller's own group is never
0691| # signalled, so a check that could not be placed in a group of its own cannot
0692| # make the cleanup reach the installer itself.
0693| signal_group() {
0694|     signal=$1
0695|     group=$2
0696|     case $group in
0697|         ''|*[!0-9]*) return 0 ;;
0698|     esac
0699|     own=
0700|     if command -v ps >/dev/null 2>&1; then
0701|         own=$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ') || own=
0702|     fi
0703|     if [ -n "$own" ] && [ "$group" = "$own" ]; then
0704|         return 0
0705|     fi
0706|     if kill -"$signal" "-$group" 2>/dev/null; then
0707|         return 0
0708|     fi
0709|     # A shell that cannot name a group signals its members one by one.
0710|     for pid in $(process_group "$group"); do
0711|         kill -"$signal" "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
0712|     done
0713|     return 0
0714| }

0716| # Stop what the checked command started. The dedicated process group is the
0717| # primary target: everything that stayed in it goes at once, on the success path
0718| # as well as on the timeout path. A sweep of the checked command's descendants
0719| # follows, so a descendant that left the group is reached as well.
0720| stop_check() {
0721|     signal=$1
0722|     signal_group "$signal" "$CHECK_GROUP"
0723|     if [ -n "$CHECK_CHILD" ]; then
0724|         for pid in $(process_tree "$CHECK_CHILD"); do
0725|             kill -"$signal" "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
0726|         done
0727|         kill -"$signal" "$CHECK_CHILD" 2>/dev/null || true
0728|     fi
0729|     return 0
0730| }

0732| # Release everything the bounded check owns: the watchdog, the checked process
0733| # group with the descendants that left it, and the private directory. It runs at
0734| # most once per check, so the exit trap and a signal trap cannot release the
0735| # same check twice and a second call is a no-op. Every piece of state the
0736| # release reads is cleared only after it has been used.
0737| cleanup_check() {
0738|     if [ -n "$CHECK_CLEANED" ]; then
0739|         return 0
0740|     fi
0741|     CHECK_CLEANED=1
0742|     if [ -n "$CHECK_WATCHER" ]; then
0743|         kill -TERM "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0744|         wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0745|         CHECK_WATCHER=
0746|     fi
0747|     if [ -n "$CHECK_GROUP" ] || [ -n "$CHECK_CHILD" ]; then
0748|         stop_check KILL
0749|         if [ -n "$CHECK_CHILD" ]; then
0750|             wait "$CHECK_CHILD" 2>/dev/null || true
0751|         fi
0752|         CHECK_GROUP=
0753|         CHECK_CHILD=
0754|     fi
0755|     if [ -n "$CHECK_DIR" ]; then
0756|         rm -rf "$CHECK_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
0757|         CHECK_DIR=
0758|     fi
0759|     return 0
0760| }

0767| # Wait, for a bounded moment, until the watchdog has recorded its decision in
0768| # the private check directory: ``timed-out`` when the bound had elapsed before
0769| # the checked command exited, ``finished`` when it saw the command gone first.
0770| # Status 0 means the decision is there, 1 that the watchdog did not answer
0771| # within DECISION_WAIT seconds. The decision says which stop to expect; it is
0772| # not the verdict, which is the time the check took (see ``bounded_run``). The
0773| # wait never depends on the checked command, so a watchdog that never answers
0774| # delays the installer by that fixed limit at most.
0775| await_decision() {
0776|     decision_dir=$1
0777|     waited=0
0778|     while :; do
0779|         if [ -e "$decision_dir/timed-out" ] || [ -e "$decision_dir/finished" ]; then
0780|             return 0
0781|         fi
0782|         if [ "$waited" -ge "$DECISION_WAIT" ]; then
0783|             return 1
0784|         fi
0785|         sleep 1 2>/dev/null || true
0786|         waited=$((waited + 1))
0787|     done
0788| }

0790| # Run a command under a hard time bound. ``timeout`` from GNU coreutils is not
0791| # required and is not used: the command runs in the background and a watchdog
0792| # stops it once the bound elapsed. The watchdog records ``timed-out`` in the
0793| # private directory before it starts the graceful stop, and ``finished`` when it
0794| # saw the command gone before the bound; that record says which stop to expect,
0795| # never what the verdict is. The installer times the check itself and reports a
0796| # timeout whenever the measured time reached the bound, so the ordering between
0797| # the command's own exit, the record and the read of the result cannot turn a
0798| # step that overran into a success. A command that finished inside the bound
0799| # keeps its own status, a nonzero one included. After the graceful stop the
0800| # watchdog forcefully stops the rest of the checked command's process group once
0801| # the grace period has passed. Nothing the function starts survives it.
0802| # CHECK_STATUS is 124 when the bound elapsed.
0803| #
0804| # The checked command leads a process group of its own (see ``start_check``), so
0805| # the group is what the cleanup signals, on the success path as much as on the
0806| # timeout path. Its three standard descriptors are redirected, so the group has
0807| # no terminal to hold it and cannot stop on a terminal access.
0808| bounded_run() {
0809|     limit=$1
0810|     shift
0811|     CHECK_STATUS=0
0812|     CHECK_OUTPUT=
0813|     CHECK_CLEANED=
0814|     CHECK_CHILD=
0815|     CHECK_GROUP=
0816|     if ! create_check_dir; then
0817|         return 1
0818|     fi
0819|     out=$CHECK_DIR/output
0820|     timed_out=$CHECK_DIR/timed-out
0821|     finished=$CHECK_DIR/finished
0822|     saved_umask=$(umask)
0823|     umask 077
0824|     if ! : > "$out"; then
0825|         umask "$saved_umask"
0826|         cleanup_check
0827|         return 1
0828|     fi
0829|     started=$(now_millis)
0830|     start_check "$out" "$@"
0831|     umask "$saved_umask"
0832|     child=$CHECK_CHILD
0833|     (
0834|         exec > /dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null
0835|         sleeper=
0836|         trap 'kill "$sleeper" 2>/dev/null || true; exit 0' TERM
0837|         elapsed=0
0838|         while [ "$elapsed" -lt "$limit" ]; do
0839|             sleep 1 &
0840|             sleeper=$!
0841|             wait "$sleeper" 2>/dev/null || true
0842|             sleeper=
0843|             elapsed=$((elapsed + 1))
0844|             if ! kill -0 "$child" 2>/dev/null; then
0845|                 # The command was gone inside the bound; record that so the
0846|                 # caller knows which stop to expect.
0847|                 : > "$finished" 2>/dev/null || true
0848|                 exit 0
0849|             fi
0850|         done
0851|         : > "$timed_out" 2>/dev/null || true
0852|         stop_check TERM
0853|         sleep "$VERIFY_GRACE" 2>/dev/null || true
0854|         stop_check KILL
0855|     ) &
0856|     CHECK_WATCHER=$!
0857|     wait "$child" || CHECK_STATUS=$?
0858|     ended=$(now_millis)
0859|     measured=$((ended - started))
0860|     if await_decision "$CHECK_DIR"; then
0861|         # The watchdog records its decision before it stops anything, so on
0862|         # the timeout path it may still own the graceful then the forceful
0863|         # stop; let it finish so nothing outlives the check.
0864|         wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0865|     else
0866|         # A watchdog that never answers is not allowed to hold the installer. A
0867|         # decision that never arrives is not evidence that the bound was kept;
0868|         # the measured time decides that below.
0869|         kill -KILL "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0870|         wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0871|     fi
0872|     # The verdict is the time the check took, never the presence of a record: a
0873|     # step that outlived the bound is a timeout even when it exited on its own
0874|     # before the timeout was recorded, and a step inside the bound keeps its own
0875|     # status, a nonzero one included.
0876|     if [ -e "$timed_out" ] || [ "$measured" -ge "$((limit * 1000))" ]; then
0877|         CHECK_STATUS=124
0878|     fi
0879|     CHECK_OUTPUT=$(cat "$out") || CHECK_OUTPUT=
0880|     # The check is released here, before any state the release reads is
0881|     # cleared: a successful check leaves nothing behind, exactly like a failed
0882|     # or a timed-out one.
0883|     cleanup_check
0884|     return 0
0885| }

1082| # Install the requested engine version through the engine's own installer.
1083| engine_install() {

1087| # The one failure report of the engine part of the run: what went wrong, the
1088| # required minimum, what was found, and the action that supplies a satisfying
1089| # engine.
1090| engine_failure() {
1091|     echo "install.sh: $1" >&2
1092|     echo "install.sh: required minimum engine version: $ENGINE_MINIMUM" >&2
1093|     if [ -n "$ENGINE_PRESENT" ]; then
1094|         echo "install.sh: engine found: $ENGINE_PRESENT" >&2
1095|     fi
1096|     if [ -n "$ENGINE_AVAILABLE" ]; then
1097|         echo "install.sh: available engine version: $ENGINE_AVAILABLE" >&2
1098|     fi
1099|     echo "install.sh: engine source: $ENGINE_SOURCE" >&2
1100|     echo "install.sh: engine installer: $ENGINE_INSTALLER" >&2
1101|     echo "install.sh: what you can do: install the Forgel engine $ENGINE_MINIMUM or newer from $ENGINE_SOURCE with the engine's own installer, point FORGEL_ENGINE_SOURCE and FORGEL_ENGINE_INSTALLER at a source that provides it, or install only the client with 'install.sh --client-only'." >&2
1102|     return 1
1103| }

1105| # Decide about the engine and reach a supported end state, or fail and say why.
1106| # The available version is read first, without installing anything, and the
1107| # present engine is never touched until that decision is made. A present engine
1108| # that already satisfies the minimum is kept whenever the offered version is not
1109| # strictly newer: nothing that is not newer is ever installed over it.
1110| install_engine() {
1111|     if ! ENGINE_MINIMUM=$(engine_minimum) || [ -z "$ENGINE_MINIMUM" ]; then
1112|         echo "install.sh: the installed client declares no minimum supported engine version" >&2
1113|         return 1
1114|     fi
1115|     ENGINE_PRESENT=
1116|     if present=$(engine_present_version); then
1117|         ENGINE_PRESENT=$present
1118|     fi
1119|     if ! ENGINE_AVAILABLE=$(engine_available_version); then
1120|         ENGINE_AVAILABLE=
1121|         engine_failure "cannot determine the engine version that $ENGINE_SOURCE provides"
1122|         return 1
1123|     fi
1124|     present_ok=0
1125|     if [ -n "$ENGINE_PRESENT" ] && version_compare ge "$ENGINE_PRESENT" "$ENGINE_MINIMUM"; then
1126|         present_ok=1
1127|     fi
1128|     if [ "$present_ok" = "1" ] && ! version_compare gt "$ENGINE_AVAILABLE" "$ENGINE_PRESENT"; then
1129|         echo "Engine: forgel $ENGINE_PRESENT kept; the available $ENGINE_AVAILABLE is not newer."
1130|         return 0
1131|     fi
1132|     if ! version_compare ge "$ENGINE_AVAILABLE" "$ENGINE_MINIMUM"; then
1133|         engine_failure "the available engine $ENGINE_AVAILABLE does not satisfy the client's minimum supported engine version"
1134|         return 1
1135|     fi
1136|     if ! engine_install "$ENGINE_AVAILABLE"; then
1137|         engine_failure "installing Forgel engine $ENGINE_AVAILABLE from $ENGINE_SOURCE failed"
1138|         return 1
1139|     fi
1140|     if [ -n "$ENGINE_PRESENT" ]; then
1141|         echo "Engine: forgel $ENGINE_AVAILABLE replaced $ENGINE_PRESENT from $ENGINE_SOURCE."
1142|     else
1143|         echo "Engine: forgel $ENGINE_AVAILABLE installed from $ENGINE_SOURCE; no engine was present."
1144|     fi
1145|     return 0
1146| }

0001| #!/bin/sh
0002| # Forgel Code installer.
0003| #
0004| # One command installs the client into a per-user prefix:
0005| #
0006| #   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh
0007| #
0008| # The client goes into ${FORGEL_CODE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share/forgel-code}, the
0009| # ``forgel-code`` launcher into ${FORGEL_CODE_BIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}, and that
0010| # directory is put on PATH through one marked block in the profile an
0011| # interactive login session of the login shell reads. The login shell is taken
0012| # from $SHELL, then from the invoking process (ps), then from the account login
0013| # shell; a shell outside the zsh and bash families gets the block in
0014| # $HOME/.profile and a warning that names the edited file. After writing the
0015| # block the installer starts that shell as a login interactive shell from a
0016| # cleared environment, in a process group of its own, under a hard time limit.
0017| # A watchdog stops that shell once the limit elapses, and the installer times
0018| # the check itself: a shell that outlived the limit fails the installation,
0019| # whatever the ordering of its own exit and the watchdog's timeout record. The
0020| # absence of a recorded timeout at the moment the check's result arrives is
0021| # never taken as evidence that the check kept its bound. Nothing the check
0022| # started outlives it: the dedicated group, and the descendants that left it,
0023| # are stopped on every exit path. The installer then checks that
0024| # ``forgel-code`` resolves to the launcher it just wrote. Re-running replaces
0025| # the installation; running with ``--uninstall`` removes it again.
0026| #
0027| # Installing the client alone is not enough to use it, so the same run also
0028| # makes sure an engine the client supports is in place. It asks the engine's own
0029| # installer which version the configured engine source provides, without
0030| # installing anything, and reads the version of an engine that is already
0031| # present. Only then does it decide: a present engine that satisfies the
0032| # client's minimum is kept when the available version is not strictly newer, a
0033| # strictly newer available engine replaces it, and an absent engine is obtained
0034| # when the available version is supported. Anything else ends the run as a
0035| # failure that names the required minimum, the version found or offered and the
0036| # action the user can take. A successful run always states the engine version in
0037| # place and how it was obtained. ``--client-only`` installs the client alone and
0038| # touches no engine. Reading a version report, and installing a version, are the
0039| # engine installer's own jobs; this script only decides and delegates.
0040| #

0001| #!/bin/sh
0002| # Forgel Code installer.
0003| #
0004| # One command installs the client into a per-user prefix:
0005| #
0006| #   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh
0007| #
0008| # The client goes into ${FORGEL_CODE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share/forgel-code}, the
0009| # ``forgel-code`` launcher into ${FORGEL_CODE_BIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}, and that
0010| # directory is put on PATH through one marked block in the profile an
0011| # interactive login session of the login shell reads. The login shell is taken
0012| # from $SHELL, then from the invoking process (ps), then from the account login
0013| # shell; a shell outside the zsh and bash families gets the block in
0014| # $HOME/.profile and a warning that names the edited file. After writing the
0015| # block the installer starts that shell as a login interactive shell from a
0016| # cleared environment, in a process group of its own, under a hard time limit.
0017| # A watchdog stops that shell once the limit elapses, and the installer times
0018| # the check itself: a shell that outlived the limit fails the installation,
0019| # whatever the ordering of its own exit and the watchdog's timeout record. The
0020| # absence of a recorded timeout at the moment the check's result arrives is
0021| # never taken as evidence that the check kept its bound. Nothing the check
0022| # started outlives it: the dedicated group, and the descendants that left it,
0023| # are stopped on every exit path. The installer then checks that
0024| # ``forgel-code`` resolves to the launcher it just wrote. Re-running replaces
0025| # the installation; running with ``--uninstall`` removes it again.
0026| #
0027| # Installing the client alone is not enough to use it, so the same run also
0028| # makes sure an engine the client supports is in place. It asks the engine's own
0029| # installer which version the configured engine source provides, without
0030| # installing anything, and reads the version of an engine that is already
0031| # present. Only then does it decide: a present engine that satisfies the
0032| # client's minimum is kept when the available version is not strictly newer, a
0033| # strictly newer available engine replaces it, and an absent engine is obtained
0034| # when the available version is supported. Anything else ends the run as a
0035| # failure that names the required minimum, the version found or offered and the
0036| # action the user can take. A successful run always states the engine version in
0037| # place and how it was obtained. ``--client-only`` installs the client alone and
0038| # touches no engine. Reading a version report, and installing a version, are the
0039| # engine installer's own jobs; this script only decides and delegates.

0041| # Environment variables:
0042| #   FORGEL_CODE_HOME            install prefix (default: $HOME/.local/share/forgel-code)
0043| #   FORGEL_CODE_BIN             launcher directory (default: $HOME/.local/bin)
0044| #   FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE          local checkout to install from, without network
0045| #   FORGEL_CODE_TAG             repository tag when no checkout is given (default: v0.2.0)

0047| #   FORGEL_CODE_PYTHON          Python 3 interpreter (default: python3 on PATH)

1607| def _alpha_runs(text: str) -> List[str]:
1608|     """The runs of letters in ``text``, in order."""
1609|     runs: List[str] = []
1610|     current: List[str] = []
1611|     for character in text:
1612|         if character.isalpha():
1613|             current.append(character)
1614|         elif current:
1615|             runs.append("".join(current))
1616|             current = []
1617|     if current:
1618|         runs.append("".join(current))
1619|     return runs

1655| def _asks_for_sensitive_action(folded: str) -> bool:
1656|     """Whether a folded sentence asks for a sensitive action in French or Spanish.
1657| 
1658|     The request needs the verb of the action and the object it acts on, in
1659|     either order; a sentence that names only one of them stays ordinary
1660|     conversation.
1661|     """
1662|     words = _alpha_runs(folded)
1663|     if not words:
1664|         return False
1665|     sequence = " " + " ".join(words) + " "
1666|     for (forms, stems), nouns in SENSITIVE_ACTIONS:
1667|         if not any(word in forms or word.startswith(stems) for word in words):
1668|             continue
1669|         if any((" " + noun + " ") in sequence for noun in nouns):
1670|             return True
1671|     return False

1692| def _elides(lowered: str) -> bool:
1693|     """Whether the text carries an elision characteristic of French."""
1694|     for index, character in enumerate(lowered):
1695|         if character not in APOSTROPHES:
1696|             continue
1697|         if index + 1 >= len(lowered) or not lowered[index + 1].isalpha():
1698|             continue
1699|         start = index
1700|         while start > 0 and lowered[start - 1].isalpha():
1701|             start -= 1
1702|         if lowered[start:index] in FRENCH_ELISIONS:
1703|             return True
1704|     return False

1707| def language_of(text: str, current: str = "en") -> str:
1708|     """The language of the owner's message, as far as a reply must follow it.
1709| 
1710|     Russian is the language of Cyrillic text, French and Spanish are recognised
1711|     by the letters, words and elisions only they use, and other Latin text is
1712|     English. A message that carries no language signal at all keeps the
1713|     language the session is already using.
1714|     """
1715|     if any("\u0400" <= character <= "\u04ff" for character in text):
1716|         return "ru"
1717|     lowered = text.lower()
1718|     french = sum(1 for character in lowered if character in FRENCH_LETTERS)
1719|     spanish = sum(1 for character in lowered if character in SPANISH_LETTERS)
1720|     for run in _alpha_runs(lowered):
1721|         if run in FRENCH_WORDS:
1722|             french += 1
1723|         elif run in SPANISH_WORDS:
1724|             spanish += 1
1725|     if _elides(lowered):
1726|         french += 1
1727|     if french > spanish:
1728|         return "fr"
1729|     if spanish > french:
1730|         return "es"
1731|     if any(len(run) > 1 for run in _alpha_runs(text)):
1732|         return "en"
1733|     return current

1806| def _phrase_end(text: str, start: int, end: int) -> Optional[int]:
1807|     """The end of a several-word secret label at ``start``, if one starts there.
1808| 
1809|     The words of such a label may be separated by any amount of whitespace, so
1810|     a line break inside it does not make the label unrecognised.
1811|     """
1812|     first = _plain(text[start:end])
1813|     for phrase in SECRET_PHRASES:
1814|         if phrase[0] != first:
1815|             continue
1816|         position = end
1817|         matched = True
1818|         for word in phrase[1:]:
1819|             after = _skip_gap(text, position)
1820|             following = _label_end(text, after)
1821|             if following is None or _plain(text[after:following]) != word:
1822|                 matched = False
1823|                 break
1824|             position = following
1825|         if matched:
1826|             return position
1827|     return None

1876| def _span(text: str, start: int) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int]]:
1877|     """The characters of the one value at ``start``, a quoted run included.
1878| 
1879|     The span is exactly what the marker replaces, so the quotation marks that
1880|     dress a value stay visible around it.
1881|     """
1882|     if start >= len(text) or text[start].isspace():
1883|         return None
1884|     if text.startswith(REDACTED, start):
1885|         return start, start + len(REDACTED)
1886|     closing = _QUOTE_PAIRS.get(text[start])
1887|     if closing is not None:
1888|         limit = len(text)
1889|         newline = text.find("\n", start)
1890|         if newline >= 0:
1891|             limit = newline
1892|         found = text.find(closing, start + 1, limit)

0003| #
0004| # One command installs the client into a per-user prefix:
0005| #
0006| #   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh
0007| #
0008| # The client goes into ${FORGEL_CODE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share/forgel-code}, the
0009| # ``forgel-code`` launcher into ${FORGEL_CODE_BIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}, and that
0010| # directory is put on PATH through one marked block in the profile an
0011| # interactive login session of the login shell reads. The login shell is taken
0012| # from $SHELL, then from the invoking process (ps), then from the account login
0013| # shell; a shell outside the zsh and bash families gets the block in
0014| # $HOME/.profile and a warning that names the edited file. After writing the
0015| # block the installer starts that shell as a login interactive shell from a
0016| # cleared environment, in a process group of its own, under a hard time limit.
0017| # A watchdog stops that shell once the limit elapses, and the installer times
0018| # the check itself: a shell that outlived the limit fails the installation,
0019| # whatever the ordering of its own exit and the watchdog's timeout record. The
0020| # absence of a recorded timeout at the moment the check's result arrives is
0021| # never taken as evidence that the check kept its bound. Nothing the check
0022| # started outlives it: the dedicated group, and the descendants that left it,
0023| # are stopped on every exit path. The installer then checks that
0024| # ``forgel-code`` resolves to the launcher it just wrote. Re-running replaces
0025| # the installation; running with ``--uninstall`` removes it again.

0028| # makes sure an engine the client supports is in place. It asks the engine's own
0029| # installer which version the configured engine source provides, without

0001| # code
0002| 
0003| Forgel Code — thin console client for Forgel over the engine's machine-readable
0004| commands.
0005| 
0006| The client does not import the engine. Its only channel is running
0007| `forgel <command> --json` as a separate process and reading exactly one JSON
0008| object from stdout. The model, sandbox, independent QA, review and release
0009| approval stay in the engine: the client never calls a model, never reads
0010| project files and never runs checks itself.
0011| 
0012| ## Install
0013| 
0014| Forgel Code installs with one command. It needs Python 3.9 or newer with the
0015| `pip` module it ships. The same run also brings the `forgel` engine the client
0016| needs onto the machine, so one command leaves a working client-and-engine pair.
0017| 
0018| ```sh
0019| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh
0020| ```
0021| 
0022| The installer puts the client into `~/.local/share/forgel-code` and a
0023| `forgel-code` launcher into `~/.local/bin`, then adds that directory to `PATH`
0024| through one marked block in the profile your login shell reads. No virtual
0025| environment and no activation step are involved, and the same command run again
0026| replaces the installation instead of duplicating anything.
0027| 
0028| | Login shell | Profile file that receives the block |
0029| | --- | --- |
0030| | zsh | `~/.zshrc` |
0031| | bash | the first existing of `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`, `~/.profile`; `~/.bash_profile` is created when none of them exists |
0032| | other POSIX `sh` | `~/.profile`, with a warning on stderr that names the file and the detected shell |
0033| 
0034| The login shell comes from `$SHELL`. When that is unset, empty or names a shell
0035| the installer does not handle, it reads the shell of the invoking process and
0036| then the account login shell — the macOS Directory Service entry, otherwise the
0037| passwd entry — and only then falls back to `~/.profile`. The block is never
0038| written to `~/.bashrc` alone, because a login bash shell does not read that
0039| file. A profile file that does not exist yet is created.
0040| 
0041| The block carries a `case "$PATH:"` guard and prepends the launcher directory
0042| only when it is not already there, so sourcing it again, or sourcing several
0043| profiles that carry it, leaves exactly one entry. There is no unguarded
0044| `export PATH=...` line.
0045| 
0046| After writing the block the installer checks it: it starts the detected login
0047| shell as a login interactive shell from a cleared environment, under a bounded
0048| time limit enforced without GNU `timeout`, and requires `command -v forgel-code`
0049| to resolve to the launcher it just wrote. On success it prints the detected
0050| shell, the edited profile file and the path that fresh shell resolved. If the
0051| check fails, or the shell does not answer within the limit, it exits non-zero
0052| and prints on stderr the edited profile file, the exact block it wrote, the
0053| shell it checked, the `PATH` that shell saw and what `forgel-code` resolved to,
0054| so a profile your login shell never reads is never reported as active.
0055| Re-running keeps exactly one marked block and leaves the rest of the file as it
0056| was.
0057| 
0058| ### The engine
0059| 
0060| The same run settles the engine the client runs. It first learns which engine
0061| version the configured engine source offers, without installing anything, and
0062| which version of an engine is already in place. Then it decides:
0063| 
0064| | Engine in place | Offered version | Result |
0065| | --- | --- | --- |
0066| | none | at or above the declared minimum | that version is installed |
0067| | at or above the minimum, and the offered version is not strictly newer | any | the engine is kept and nothing about it is changed |
0068| | below the offered version | supported and strictly newer | the strictly newer version replaces the engine in place |
0069| 
0070| A version equal to, or older than, the one in place is never installed. The
0071| engine versions are ordered numerically, component by component; one leading
0072| version prefix and trailing zero components do not change the comparison, and a
0073| version that cannot be ordered never counts as supported. The engine left in
0074| place always satisfies the client's declared minimum supported engine version;
0075| when that cannot be reached the run ends as a failure instead of reporting the
0076| pair as installed: the offered version is below the minimum and no suitable
0077| engine is present, the engine source cannot be read, or installing the engine
0078| fails. The failure message names the required minimum, the engine version found
0079| or offered, and what you can do next. A successful run states the engine version
0080| in place and how it was obtained: installed, kept or replaced.
0081| 
0082| ### Engine source
0083| 
0084| The engine source the run resolves against is configuration with a default, and
0085| either variable can point it elsewhere.
0086| 
0087| | Variable | Effect |
0088| | --- | --- |
0089| | `FORGEL_ENGINE_SOURCE` | engine source the run asks about and installs from (default `https://github.com/forgel-dev/forgel`) |
0090| | `FORGEL_ENGINE_INSTALLER` | the engine's own installer the run asks and delegates to (default `forgel-install` on `PATH`) |
0091| 
0092| ```sh
0093| FORGEL_ENGINE_SOURCE=https://example.test/forgel-mirror sh install.sh
0094| ```
0095| 
0096| ### Client only
0097| 
0098| ```sh
0099| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh -s -- --client-only
0100| ```
0101| 
0102| installs the client alone. That route neither queries nor installs nor changes
0103| any engine, and an engine present beforehand stays exactly as it was. The
0104| engine is then yours to supply, at the client's declared minimum supported
0105| engine version or newer, before you use the client.
0106| 
0107| The client has no dependencies and builds through the small in-tree PEP 517
0108| backend (`_build_backend.py`), so the installer never needs a package index.
0109| Editable installs are not supported: the backend implements only the
0110| `build_wheel` and `build_sdist` hooks.
0111|

0968| def _recording_login_shell(directory: Path, probe: Path, real_shell: str) -> Path:
0969|     """A handled shell name that records the check's directory, then runs ``real_shell``.
0970| 
0971|     ``ls -ld`` output of every ``forgel-code-check.*`` entry goes into ``probe``,
0972|     so the test can inspect the permissions of a directory that no longer exists
0973|     by the time the installer returns. The entries sit in the temporary tree of
0974|     the test, next to the checked shell's own ``$HOME``.
0975|     """
0976|     directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
0977|     stub = directory / "bash"
0978|     stub.write_text(
0979|         "#!/bin/sh\nprobe=%s\n" % _shell_quote(probe)
0980|         + 'ls -ld "$(dirname "$HOME")/tmp"/%s.* > "$probe/entries" 2>/dev/null || true\n'
0981|         % CHECK_PREFIX
0982|         + 'exec %s "$@"\n' % _shell_quote(real_shell),
0983|         encoding="utf-8",
0984|     )
0985|     stub.chmod(0o755)
0986|     return stub

0989| def _late_login_shell(directory: Path, launcher: Path) -> Path:
0990|     """A handled shell that answers past the bound but claims the launcher resolved.
0991| 
0992|     Its login session sleeps past a one-second bound and then prints exactly the
0993|     report a successful check prints. It ignores the graceful stop, so its own
0994|     exit, and not a signal, is what ends it.
0995|     """
0996|     directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
0997|     stub = directory / "bash"
0998|     stub.write_text(
0999|         "#!/bin/sh\n"
1000|         "trap '' TERM\n"
1001|         "sleep 2\n"
1002|         "printf 'forgel-fresh-path=%s\\n' '/usr/bin:/bin'\n"
1003|         "printf 'forgel-fresh-resolved=%s\\n' " + _shell_quote(launcher) + "\n"
1004|         "exit 0\n",
1005|         encoding="utf-8",
1006|     )
1007|     stub.chmod(0o755)
1008|     return stub
1009|

1011| def _late_login_shell_withholding_decision(directory: Path, launcher: Path) -> Path:
1012|     """A late shell that hides the watchdog's decision while it runs.
1013| 
1014|     It removes the write permission of the private check directory, so the
1015|     watchdog cannot record whether the bound elapsed, and restores it when it
1016|     exits past the bound, still printing the report of a successful check. The
1017|     directory is found the way the permission probe finds it: under the TMPDIR
1018|     the installer was given, next to the checked shell's own ``$HOME``.
1019|     """
1020|     directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1021|     stub = directory / "bash"
1022|     stub.write_text(
1023|         "#!/bin/sh\n"
1024|         "trap '' TERM\n"
1025|         "check_dir=\n"
1026|         'for candidate in "$(dirname "$HOME")/tmp"/%s.*; do\n' % CHECK_PREFIX
1027|         + '    [ -d "$candidate" ] || continue\n'
1028|         + "    check_dir=$candidate\n"
1029|         + '    chmod 500 "$candidate" 2>/dev/null || true\n'
1030|         + "done\n"
1031|         + "sleep 2\n"
1032|         + "printf 'forgel-fresh-path=%s\\n' '/usr/bin:/bin'\n"
1033|         + "printf 'forgel-fresh-resolved=%s\\n' " + _shell_quote(launcher) + "\n"
1034|         + 'if [ -n "$check_dir" ]; then\n'
1035|         + '    chmod 700 "$check_dir" 2>/dev/null || true\n'
1036|         + "fi\n"
1037|         + "exit 0\n",
1038|         encoding="utf-8",
1039|     )
1040|     stub.chmod(0o755)
1041|     return stub

0497|                         terminate = 0

0499|                         terminate = 0

0521| # Exactly one block, whatever the profile already held. The previous block is
0522| # removed first and only then is the new one appended, so an interrupted run

0524| # same profile rewrites it to the same bytes, and a last line without a final
0525| # newline is recorded so the block can be dropped without leaving a newline

0562| # The current time in milliseconds, so the check can be timed. A ``date`` with
0563| # nanoseconds answers with them; one without that extension (macOS writes the
0564| # literal ``N``) falls back to the interpreter the installer already requires,

0566| # clock reports 0, and the verdict is then the recorded timeout alone.
0567| now_millis() {

0580|         esac
0581|         if [ -n "$stamp" ]; then
0582|             printf '%s\n' "$stamp"
0583|             return 0
0584|         fi
0585|     fi
0586|     stamp=$(date +%s 2>/dev/null) || stamp=
0587|     case $stamp in
0588|         ''|*[!0-9]*) stamp=0 ;;
0589|     esac
0590|     printf '%s\n' "$((stamp * 1000))"
